# `mbx reservations`

- **Usage:** `mbx reservations <SOCKET>`

Serve reservations of the scheduler pool on a Unix socket until standard input closes.

For a runner that starts many external commands, such as an Nx run's tasks: it starts this once instead of one `mbx reserve` per command. A client connects and sends newline-delimited JSON: `{"type":"reserve","id":1,"cpus":4,"priority":"low"}` (optionally with `"memory"` in bytes) is answered `{"type":"granted","id":1,"cpus":K}` once the pool admits it, `K` being as many of those cores as were free, at least one, or `{"type":"refused","id":1,"error":"..."}`. `{"type":"release","id":1}` gives the grant back, or withdraws it while it waits. One connection may hold many grants under distinct ids, and closing it releases all of them, so a client that dies gives back what it held. A line that breaks the protocol is answered `{"type":"error","error":"..."}` and closes the connection.

Admission is `mbx reserve`'s: the same pool, priorities and order. mbx creates the socket readable only by its user, prints `listening` once it accepts connections, and removes the socket when it exits.

## Arguments
- **`<SOCKET>`** — Unix socket to listen on. It must not exist yet: mbx creates it, readable and writable only by its user, and removes it when it exits.

## Flags
- **`-h --help`** — Print help
